content.section_title: 10.3 Strategies for patient follow-up after pulmonary embolism
content.follow_up_timing: Follow-up at 3–6 months after acute PE
primary_goals_of_follow_up: Assess persistence or new onset and severity of dyspnoea or functional limitation
Check for signs of VTE recurrence
Check for bleeding complications of anticoagulation

diagnostic_workup_pathway_summary.initial_step: Assess presence of dyspnoea and/or functional limitation
if_dyspnoea_or_functional_limitation_pre: Perform transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) to determine probability of pulmonary hypertension (PH)
Consider NT-proBNP and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) as part of evaluation
Classify probability of PH (low/intermediate/high) and act accordingly
diagnostic_workup_pathway_summary.if_no_dyspnoea/functional_limitation: Assess risk factors for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH); if none present focus on anticoagulation and secondary prophylaxis and advise return if symptoms appear
further_testing_if_high_probability_or_a: Ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) scan to look for mismatched perfusion defects
If V/Q shows mismatched perfusion defects, refer to PH/CTEPH expert centre for further diagnostic work‑up
diagnostic_workup_pathway_summary.alternative_paths: If low probability of PH, seek alternative causes of dyspnoea and common causes of PH

key_recommendations_and_notes: Use standardized scales (MRC / WHO) to evaluate dyspnoea
NT-proBNP and abnormal CPET results are listed among considerations when determining further workup
Risk factors and predisposing conditions for CTEPH are referenced (Table 13) but not shown on this page
Refer to ESC/ERS guidelines on diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension for definitions and further details
